prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you have a specific type of work (kitchen/bath remodel, whole-house remodel, roof, foundation, HVAC, general repairs) and a target timeline or budget? That will let me suggest the best local specialties and the right contractors to contact.

Until you tell me more, here are practical next steps and resources to quickly find a reliable Joplin, MO contractor plus a vetting checklist and a short message you can send to prospective contractors.

Where to search for local contractors
- Google Maps/Google Business Profile (reviews and recent photos)
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) — business rating, complaints history
- Angi (formerly Angie's List), HomeAdvisor, Houzz — project photos and reviews
- Local Facebook community groups, Nextdoor — neighborhood recommendations
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce — member contractors
- Local hardware stores/building-supply yards — they often know reputable contractors
- Trade-specific licensing boards: electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians often have searchable state/local license lookup

Important vetting checklist
1. Licensing & insurance
   - Verify any required trade licenses (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) and ask for proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp.
   - Confirm whether the contractor will pull required city/county permits (ask to see pulled-permit copies).
2. References & portfolio
   - Ask for 3 recent local references and photos of completed projects similar to yours. Call those references.
3. Written estimate & contract
   - Get at least three written bids with itemized scopes (materials, labor, timeline).
   - Contract should include start/end dates, payment schedule, change order process, cleanup, warranties.
4. Payment terms
   - Avoid large upfront cash payments. Common deposits range 10–30% with final payment on completion and after lien waivers.
5. Timeline & communication
   - Confirm expected work schedule and daily cleanup. Ask how they handle delays and subcontractors.
6. Red flags
   - Unwillingness to provide references or written contract, strong pressure for full cash up front, no business address, poor online reviews citing the same issues repeatedly.

Sample message to send to contractors (copy/paste)
Hello — I’m planning a [brief description: e.g., full kitchen remodel / roof replacement / bathroom update / drywall repairs after storm damage] at my home in Joplin. Could you provide availability and a ballpark estimate, and tell me if you are licensed/insured and able to pull required permits? I’d also like to see a sample contract and references for similar local jobs. Thanks — [Your name and phone]

If you’d like, I can:
- Help you draft a more detailed RFP (scope of work) to send to multiple contractors.
- Review up to 3 written estimates/quotes (you can paste them here) and point out differences and potential issues.
- Provide a short list of contractors if you tell me the exact project type; I’ll include what to ask each one.

Tell me the type of project, your timeline, and whether you prefer general remodelers or trade-specific pros, and I’ll tailor recommendations.
